description: FIRETRACK is an independent project team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are developing a satellite-based platform to explore and compare MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations. Our goal is to make burning activity easier to understand through interactive maps, data visualizations, historical analysis, and transparent scientific methods.
summary: FIRETRACK is a web-based platform designed to help users explore and analyse active-fire hotspot data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments. It focuses on Area of Interest (AOI)-based analysis, historical fire activity, temporal patterns, and the comparison of satellite detections. By bringing these data and visualisations together, FIRETRACK aims to make fire activity information easier to explore and interpret while communicating important data-coverage and scientific limitations.
details:
FIRETRACK — Exploring Fire Activity Through Satellite Data

Wildfires and other fire events can have significant environmental and social impacts. Satellite active-fire products provide valuable information about thermal anomalies, but comparing observations from different satellite instruments and understanding their availability over a selected region can be challenging.

FIRETRACK is a web-based project developed to make MODIS and VIIRS active-fire hotspot information easier to explore through a unified interface.

Users can work with a selected Area of Interest (AOI) and explore available hotspot records across different dates. The project is designed to bring together spatial and temporal analysis, a burning-activity calendar, historical visualisations, and comparisons between satellite datasets.

Its intended capabilities include:

  • AOI-based exploration of active-fire detections.
  • MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data integration.
  • Spatial and temporal analysis of detections.
  • Historical activity visualisation.
  • Calendar-based exploration of activity over time.
  • Comparison of detections from different satellite instruments.
  • Anomaly exploration where sufficient evidence is available.
  • Clear presentation of data availability and coverage limitations.

An important design principle of FIRETRACK is scientific transparency. Missing data must not be interpreted as zero fire activity. A successful data query with no detections does not, by itself, prove that a satellite observed the entire area or that conditions were cloud-free. Active-fire detections are thermal anomalies and should not automatically be interpreted as confirmed wildfires.

FIRETRACK aims to make satellite fire information more accessible and understandable while helping users recognise the limitations of the underlying observations.

Challenge relevance: The project addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge concerning harmonisation of MODIS and VIIRS hotspots by focusing on combined exploration, AOI-based analysis, historical activity and responsible interpretation of satellite detections.
